h1: The 5 Best Lawn Mowers for Uneven Ground and Slopes, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Lawn Mowers for Uneven Ground: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 5 mowers for hilly and bumpy lawns, compared on drive type, deck size, power source, robot slope rating and price.
mainKeyword: best lawn mowers for uneven ground
summary: The EGO POWER+ 21 inch self-propelled is the best mower for uneven ground, combining cordless convenience with powered drive. Segway's Navimow X430 is the best robot for slopes, Greenworks 80V is the value cordless pick, and PowerSmart's rear-wheel-drive gas model is the best hill climber on fuel.
intro: Uneven ground punishes the wrong mower in two ways. A wide deck scalps humps, and an undriven machine tires you out on slopes. Most buyers shop by engine size and miss the two specs that matter: which wheels are driven and how wide the deck is. The test for a rough lawn is traction first, cutting width second, and only then power.

We ranked five mowers for rolling and bumpy lawns by drive type, deck width, power source and price, plus one robot with a stated slope rating. Listing data is uneven, and we say so where the drive layout or battery runtime is not given. Where a listing leaves out a spec such as the driven axle, we say so.

products.name: EGO POWER+ 21-Inch Cordless Self-Propelled Mower LM2135SP
products.verdict: A cordless self-propelled 21 inch mower with the battery and charger in the box.
products.description:
The EGO LM2135SP is a 21 inch cordless mower with a self-propelled drive and a battery and charger included. It is in the $500+ tier, the top of this ranking's price range.

On uneven ground, drive matters more than deck size. A self-propelled mower pulls itself up humps and slows on downhill runs so you are not wrestling 60-odd pounds of machine. EGO puts that in a cordless body, which removes the starting and fuel chores that come with the gas models below it.

It is the pick for a half-acre lawn with rolling terrain and a sensitive back. The cost is the price tag, and with no run-time figure listed, a large lawn may need a second battery.
products.idealFor: Rolling half-acre lawns and users who dislike gas engines.

products.name: Segway Navimow X430 Robot Lawn Mower
products.verdict: A wire-free, four-wheel-drive robot rated for 84 percent slopes and up to 1 acre.
products.description:
The Navimow X430 is a robot mower with wire-free navigation for lawns up to 1 acre, 4WD and dual 180W motors, rated for slopes up to 84 percent. It is in the $500+ tier.

Robots solve uneven ground by never tiring, and four-wheel drive is what lets a robot climb where a two-wheel unit spins. The wire-free system avoids burying a boundary cable, which is the usual setup headache. Against the EGO it gives up the manual control, and you must still clear sticks and rocks beforehand.

Buy it if you want a hands-off lawn. Skip it for a lot with steep drop-offs near water or a road, because a rated slope is not a promise at the edge of a bank.
products.idealFor: Hilly lawns where you want mowing fully automated.
products.skipIf: Your lawn has steep banks near hazards.

products.name: Greenworks 80V 21-Inch Self-Propelled Mower
products.verdict: Self-propelled, 80V and a 4.0Ah battery in the box, at the mid price tier.
products.description:
The Greenworks 80V is a 21 inch self-propelled cordless mower that includes a 4.0Ah battery and charger. It costs between $200 and $500. 80V is a higher-voltage platform than typical 40V packs.

It sits below the EGO because it sits in a cheaper price class and lists less detail, but the 80V battery platform is a strong one and the self-propelled drive is the key feature for slopes. It saves hundreds over the top pick for the same deck size.

Buy it for a quarter to half acre with moderate bumps. A 4.0Ah pack can run short on thick or damp grass, so plan to mow in sections or buy a second battery. Keep the second pack charged for a long session.
cons: 4.0Ah may run short on large lots
products.idealFor: Quarter to half acre lawns with moderate bumps.
products.skipIf: You mow a large lot on one charge.

products.name: PowerSmart 21-Inch Self-Propelled Gas Mower for Hills
products.verdict: A 170cc OHV gas engine with rear-wheel drive and six height settings.
products.description:
PowerSmart's hill-focused mower has a 21 inch alloy steel deck, a 170cc OHV engine, rear-wheel drive and a 6-position height adjustment. It costs between $200 and $500. Alloy steel resists dents from stumps and stones.

Rear-wheel drive is what you want on slopes, because the driven wheels press harder when you push uphill and keep their grip. A front-wheel-drive unit lifts its drive wheels on a climb and loses traction. That is why this mower belongs here even though it is gas. Six height positions help ride over bumps.

Buy it for rough, hilly ground where running time is not a concern. Gas engines need fuel, oil and spring tune-ups, so factor that against the cordless EGO and Greenworks.
products.idealFor: Hilly, rough lawns where run time matters.
products.skipIf: You want a quiet, no-fuel mower.

products.name: SENIX 201cc 22-Inch Self-Propelled Gas Mower
products.verdict: A 201cc engine, 22 inch deck and variable-speed drive with 3-in-1 mulch, bag and discharge.
products.description:
The SENIX has a 201cc engine, a 22 inch deck, variable-speed self-propelled drive and 3-in-1 mulch, bag and discharge. It sits at $200 to $500. Variable speed helps pace yourself on a slope.

It ranks below the PowerSmart hill mower on traction design because the listing does not state the driven axle. What it adds is power and speed control: a larger engine holds blade speed in thick or wet grass, and variable speed lets you slow down on a slope.

Buy it for large, thick lawns with gentle unevenness. Check the drive layout before buying for steep banks. A 22 inch deck is the practical maximum for rolling ground.
products.idealFor: Thick, large lawns with gentle bumps.

whatMatters.detail: Drive wheels are the wheels that pull the mower. Rear-wheel drive presses the driven wheels down as you climb, which keeps traction on a slope. Front-wheel drive unloads on a climb and slips. Look in the listing for the driven axle, as the PowerSmart hill model states, and avoid push-only mowers on steep ground where you carry the weight.

Deck width decides how the mower rides over bumps. A wide deck bridges small dips but its edges dig into the crown of each hump and scalp the grass down to dirt. A 21 inch deck suits rolling lawns and 22 inches is the practical upper limit. On rough ground, raise the cutting height a notch to avoid cutting dirt.

Cordless versus gas is a choice of upkeep. Cordless mowers start at a button and are quiet but depend on battery capacity, like the 4.0Ah pack with the Greenworks. Gas runs until the tank is empty but needs fuel, oil changes and spark plug checks. Choose by lawn size, runtime needs and how much maintenance you accept.

A robot slope rating is the steepest grade a robot mower can climb. The Navimow X430 is rated for 84 percent slopes with four-wheel drive. A rating is a limit, not a target, and wet grass reduces it. Keep a margin, fence off steep banks and ditches, and check that the rated grade matches your steepest patch.

Height adjustment lets you ride over humps and trim to a clean finish. Positions give you control: more positions mean finer steps between scalping and a close cut. The PowerSmart hills model lists six. Look for at least five on a rough lawn, and raise one step before mowing a hill for the first time.

faq.q: Will a self-propelled mower handle my slope?
faq.a: On moderate slopes, yes. The PowerSmart hills model has rear-wheel drive, and the Navimow X430 is rated for 84 percent. On steep banks, mow across the slope with care or trim by hand, since a rating is not a guarantee on wet grass.
Buying a wide deck for a bumpy lawn. A 22 inch deck like the SENIX's bridges dips but scalps each hump, so raise the height setting. A 21 inch deck such as the EGO or Greenworks is the safer width.

faq.q: Is a robot worth it over a push mower?
faq.a: For hilly lawns up to 1 acre, the Navimow saves hours, though it still needs a clear lawn and occasional edge trimming. A self-propelled EGO or Greenworks keeps you in control and costs less, but you still do the walking.

faq.q: How do I set up the robot?
faq.a: The Navimow is wire-free, so you map the boundary in the app rather than burying a cable. Clear sticks, toys and rocks first, then walk the edges and mark no-go zones near drop-offs and water.

Cordless units like the EGO and Greenworks need blade sharpening and battery care, so store packs indoors. Gas models like the SENIX and PowerSmart need fresh fuel, oil changes and spark plug checks each season.
Avoid it. Wet grass clogs the deck, cuts slope traction and can slip even a rear-drive PowerSmart or a four-wheel Navimow. Wait until the lawn dries, or mow at midday on a dry slope.

finalTake: The EGO POWER+ is the mower to buy for uneven ground if you want cordless, and PowerSmart's 21 inch rear-wheel-drive is the gas answer for hills. Segway's Navimow suits hands-off owners and Greenworks 80V is the value pick. Check which wheels are driven before you buy anything.
